children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask you some questions. Let's start with your child.

**Do you have a child you're claiming for? If yes, how old are they?**

The age of the child is important because:
- Children under 16 may automatically qualify
- Young people aged 16-19 may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Those aged 20 or over generally don't qualify

Please tell me the age of the child (or children) you want to claim Child Benefit for.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 15 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're looking to claim Child Benefit for your son Alex, who is 15 years old and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is under 16, let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now, the next question:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

In other words, is he either not working at all, or working part-time for less than 24 hours per week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's still in school full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is still in school and not working. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

In other words, is Alex receiving Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit in his own name (not as part of your family claim)?

Most 15-year-olds don't receive these benefits in their own right, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a regular schoolkid.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. Let me continue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Next question:

**Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship?**

Since he's in school full-time, I'm assuming he's not in an apprenticeship, but I need to confirm. Certain types of apprenticeships can affect Child Benefit eligibility depending on where you live (England, Scotland, or Wales).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. He's just doing his regular school studies.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is just in regular school, not an apprenticeship. Let me continue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check your residency status.

**Do you meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit?**

You qualify if ANY of the following applies to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** - this is the most common scenario
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and meet certain conditions (working, studying, or have sufficient resources)
4. You're a Crown servant living abroad

**Do you normally live in the UK?** This would be the straightforward answer for most claimants.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm based in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You live in the UK (Manchester), so you meet the residency requirements. Let me continue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You mentioned earlier that Alex lives at home with you, which means you meet this requirement. You're considered responsible if ANY of these apply:

1. **You live with the child** (which you've already told me Alex does)
2. You contribute to their upkeep (paying for food, clothes, housing, etc.)
3. You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement

Since Alex lives with you at home, you clearly meet this requirement. Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. Alex lives at home with me, so I'm responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You're responsible for Alex as he lives with you. Let me continue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about other potential claimants.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member or guardian
- Anyone else who might be responsible for Alex

Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at a time. If someone else is claiming, you would need to arrange for them to stop claiming before you can start.

Is there anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! No one else is claiming for Alex. Let me continue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's living situation.

**Which of the following best describes Alex's current living situation?**

- Is Alex in hospital?
- Is Alex in local authority care?
- Is Alex fostered?
- Or is Alex living normally at home with you?

You mentioned Alex lives at home with you, so I'm assuming it's the normal living situation, but I need to confirm there are no special circumstances like hospital stays or care arrangements.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is just living normally at home with me. He's not in hospital, not in care, and not fostered.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally at home with you. Let me continue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! One final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the council providing any financial support specifically for Alex's housing costs or living expenses? Since Alex lives at home with you and you're responsible for him, I'm assuming the council is not paying for his accommodation or maintenance, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - the council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. I'm covering all his costs myself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Let me process the final outcome.

conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News - You're ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit!

**Result:** You meet all the eligibility requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

### Why You're Eligible:

Based on our assessment:
✅ Alex is 15 years old (under 16)
✅ He's not working 24+ hours per week
✅ He's not receiving benefits in his own right
✅ He's not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
✅ You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
✅ You're responsible for Alex as he lives at home with you
✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
✅ Alex is living normally at home
✅ The local council is not paying towards his accommodation or maintenance

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or your partner earns over £60,000, you may need to pay some or all of the benefit back through your tax return
5. **Payments** are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

### How to Apply:

You can find full details on how to claim here: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit or the claiming process?
